title: Support step packager and playbook runtime
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: On-call engineers and SREs repeatedly author ad-hoc scripts and one-off runbook steps. These are hard to review, non-idempotent, and have inconsistent telemetry. We need a small packaging/runtime layer that converts curated support steps into versioned, idempotent packages that can be executed in the ops runtime, dry-run in sandboxes, and surfaced in the Console as ‘executable tasks’.

Objective: Build a minimal 'Support Step Packager' and accompanying lightweight Playbook Runtime that: (1) standardizes input schemas and preconditions, (2) enforces idempotency primitives and safety checks, (3) emits structured telemetry and provenance, and (4) supports dry-run and gradual rollout in production. This is aimed at reducing MTTI for common incidents and making repairs auditable and revertible.
acceptance_criteria: CLI tool or Make target that packages a support-step directory into a .ssp (support step package) with metadata and a content hash
Packaged steps include: schema.json (input schema), preflight.sh (checks), execute.sh (idempotent action), revert.sh (optional), and metadata.yaml (version, owner, tags)
Playbook Runtime can execute .ssp in a sandbox mode (--dry-run) validating inputs and printing a plan without mutating resources
Playbook Runtime supports a safety flag (--require-approval) and runtime enforcement of environment whitelists and rate limits
Console UI shows package version, last run, run duration, cost estimate token, and a link to the execution log
Telemetry generated for each run: package_id, version, inputs_hash, outcome (success/failed/rolled_back), duration_ms, tokens_consumed, and exec_nodes touched
Rollout policy: 10% canary traffic -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback on failure >3% within 30m
Documentation and example library with 6 curated packages (DB-rotate-key, cache-warm, model-restart-safe, revoke-session, infra-tagging, gather-diagnostics)
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 wks): Design metadata schema, CLI prototype packaging format, and a minimal sandboxed runtime that validates schema.json and runs preflight checks
Phase 2 (3 wks): Implement idempotency helpers (locking, read-before-write checks), telemetry hooks, and replay-safe logging format; integrate with uploads to Console artifact store
Phase 3 (2 wks): Add dry-run mode, approval gating, and rollout config; build Console surface (read-only first) and link to logs
Phase 4 (1 wk): Populate curated package library, create docs, run beta with oncall team and one customer-impacting playbook under supervision
tasks: Define .ssp package layout and metadata fields (schema, metadata, scripts)
Prototype packager CLI (go/python) with --validate and --package flags
Implement runtime with sandboxing and configurable shims for secrets and API keys
Add telemetry emitter and ensure logs are correlated with request traces
Create Console read-only artifact view and execution history panel
Write 6 curated example packages and add to infra repo
Write playbook for beta run with oncall and document rollback procedure
Security review and threat model of runtime execution surface
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Packaged steps could accidentally perform destructive actions. Mitigation: default to dry-run; require explicit --danger flag and approval gating for actions that match destructive patterns.
Risk: Secrets exposure in packaged scripts. Mitigation: runtime will never surface secrets; support environment variable injection via KMS-backed ephemeral tokens and audit every injection event.
Risk: Non-idempotent third-party scripts. Mitigation: provide idempotency library (lock/unlock, check-state functions) and require implementer to list side-effect APIs in metadata for review.
Risk: Telemetry overhead and cost. Mitigation: batch telemetry and include sampling controls per package, surfaced in metadata.
